label: Bhadla Solar Park
sub: 2,700 MW — World's largest solar park (Rajasthan, India). Operational since 2020.

label: Hornsea 2 Offshore Wind
sub: 1,386 MW — World's largest offshore wind farm at construction. Located in the North Sea, UK. Won contract at £39.65/MWh in 2019.

label: Jiuquan Wind Power Base
sub: 20,000 MW planned — Gansu Province, China. Largest wind energy base in the world. Core of China's western renewable supergrid.

label: Noor Solar Complex
sub: 580 MW CSP + PV — Ouarzazate, Morocco. Africa's largest solar facility; integrates 3-hour molten salt thermal storage.

label: Hellisheidi Geothermal
sub: 303 MW electric / 400 MW heat — Iceland's largest power plant; powers Reykjavik. Site co-located with Climeworks carbon capture plant.

label: Climeworks Mammoth (DAC)
sub: 36,000 tCO₂/yr — World's largest direct air capture plant, opened May 2024. CO₂ mineralizes in basalt rock permanently.

label: Drax BECCS Pilot (UK)
sub: Yorkshire, UK. Drax Power Station is piloting bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS) — capturing CO₂ from biomass combustion. Planned for full operation in late 2020s.

label: Boundary Dam CCS
sub: Saskatchewan, Canada. World's first commercial post-combustion CCS on a coal power plant, operational 2014. Captures ~1 MtCO₂/yr when running at capacity.

label: Tesla Gigafactory 1
sub: Sparks, Nevada, USA. World's largest battery manufacturing facility; produces ~100 GWh/yr of Li-ion cells for Tesla vehicles and Powerwall storage.

label: VW PowerCo Gigafactory
sub: Salzgitter, Germany. Volkswagen's first in-house battery cell gigafactory, part of €20B plan for 6 European battery plants by 2030. Anchors Europe's battery supply chain transition.

label: EU Green Deal HQ (Brussels)
sub: European Commission headquarters. Origin of the European Green Deal (2019), EU Climate Law (2021), Fit for 55 package, and REPowerEU — the world's most comprehensive climate legislation.

label: COP21 — Paris Agreement
sub: Le Bourget, Paris, France. Site of COP21 (Dec 2015) where 195 nations adopted the Paris Agreement — the central framework for global climate action.

label: COP28 — Dubai Consensus
sub: Expo City Dubai, UAE. COP28 (Nov–Dec 2023) produced the first global pledge to 'transition away from fossil fuels' and commitments to triple renewables + double efficiency by 2030.

label: Lake Turkana Wind Farm
sub: 310 MW — Kenya. Africa's largest wind farm (310 turbines), supplying ~17% of Kenya's installed grid capacity. Reduces diesel generation, cutting both cost and emissions.

label: Amazon REDD+ Zone
sub: Amazonas State, Brazil. Core zone for forest protection under REDD+ and Brazil's Amazon Fund ($3.8B pledged by Norway, Germany, USA). H1 2026 deforestation (1,295 km²) is the lowest since 2016, down 38% YoY; rolling 12-month total is the lowest since DETER records began in 2014.

label: Great Green Wall
sub: Dakar, Senegal. Anchor site of Africa's Great Green Wall — a 8,000 km belt of trees across the Sahel from Senegal to Djibouti. Aims to restore 100M ha of degraded land by 2030.

label: Three Gorges Dam
sub: 22,500 MW — Yichang, Hubei, China. World's largest hydropower plant; generates ~100 TWh/yr, displacing ~50 Mt CO₂ annually vs equivalent coal generation.

label: Kamuthi Solar Power Plant
sub: 648 MW — Tamil Nadu, India. Built in just 8 months in 2016; was the world's largest single-location solar plant at time of completion. Self-cleaning robotic panels.

label: El Romero Solar (Atacama)
sub: 246 MW — Atacama Desert, Chile. Chile leads Latin America in solar with some of the world's highest irradiation. Chile hit 30% renewable electricity by 2022.

label: Bonn Challenge Coordination
sub: Bonn, Germany. Origin of the Bonn Challenge (2011) — global goal to restore 350 million hectares of deforested land by 2030. Over 73 pledging nations and organizations have committed 210M+ ha.

label: COP30 — Belém Package
sub: Belém, Brazil. COP30 (November 2025) adopted the 'Belém Package' — 29 decisions including a Just Transition mechanism, commitment to triple adaptation finance by 2035, and Brazil's Tropical Forest Forever Facility (USD 125B blended-finance fund). First COP held in the Amazon.

label: EU 2040 Climate Law (90%)
sub: Brussels, Belgium. EU Regulation 2026/667 entered into force April 7, 2026 — the world's most ambitious legally binding medium-term climate target: 90% net GHG reduction by 2040 vs. 1990. Trajectory: −55% (2030) → −90% (2040) → net-zero (2050).

label: Santa Marta Fossil Fuel Conference
sub: Santa Marta, Colombia. Site of the First International Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels (April 24–29, 2026), co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands. 60+ nations attended; Science Panel for Global Energy Transition (SPGET) launched here by Johan Rockström and Carlos Nobre. First summit dedicated to fossil fuel phase-out, operating outside UNFCCC framework.

label: Duke Energy SMR Permit (Belews Creek)
sub: Stokes County, North Carolina, USA. Duke Energy filed an initial site permit for a Small Modular Reactor (SMR) at Belews Creek on April 25, 2026, as part of its record $103B five-year capital plan. The first regulated US utility to formally advance SMR licensing — driven by surging AI data center electricity demand and decarbonization commitments.

label: EMYN Offshore Wind (500 MW)
sub: Atlantic Ocean off Yeu & Noirmoutier islands, Vendée, France. France's largest offshore wind farm — 61 turbines, 500 MW, fully operational May 6, 2026. Powers ~800,000 homes. Built by Ocean Winds (ENGIE/EDP Renewables JV). A milestone for France's offshore wind sector after years of permitting delays.

label: EFGL Floating Wind (30 MW pilot)
sub: Gulf of Lion, 16 km off Port-la-Nouvelle, Occitanie, France. France's first floating offshore wind farm — 3 × 10 MW turbines on semi-submersible foundations. First power to grid May 5, 2026. Produces ~110,000 MWh/yr. Developed by Ocean Winds (ENGIE/EDP Renewables), paving the way for commercial-scale floating wind in the Mediterranean.

label: India 50% Non-Fossil Power
sub: India, May 2026. India surpassed 50% non-fossil installed electricity capacity — 5 years ahead of its 2030 Paris Agreement target. Total non-fossil capacity: 254+ GW including 150 GW solar, 50+ GW wind. Record 55.3 GW added in FY 2025-26. World's 3rd largest renewable market.

label: Ford Energy BESS Factory (Kentucky)
sub: Glendale, Kentucky, USA. Ford Energy launched May 2026 — repurposed former BlueOval SK EV battery plant for grid-scale BESS. Target: 20 GWh/yr of US-assembled LFP battery storage systems for utilities and data centers. Flagship DC Block product (512 Ah LFP, 2-hr/4-hr configurations); $2B investment.

label: Africa Forward Summit (Nairobi)
sub: Nairobi, Kenya. May 11–12, 2026. Kenya–France bilateral summit advancing Africa's green industrialization. 11 clean energy and infrastructure agreements signed; France–Kenya coalition launched €187B luxury air travel levy for climate finance in developing nations. Kenya generates 90%+ electricity from renewables.

label: Northern Lights CCS (Øygarden)
sub: Øygarden, Norway. World's first open-access CO₂ transport and storage facility — Equinor, Shell, TotalEnergies JV. Stores CO₂ 2,600 m below the North Sea seabed. Phase 1: 1.5 Mt CO₂/yr. First injection August 2025; commercial operations 2026. Yara Sluiskil (Netherlands) is the first commercial customer: 800,000 t CO₂/yr from fertilizer production.

label: Barrow Green Hydrogen (30 MW)
sub: Barrow-in-Furness, Cumbria, UK. 30 MW Plug Power PEM electrolyzer project — FID reached May 2026. Produces ~100 GWh/yr green hydrogen for Kimberly-Clark manufacturing, cutting site natural gas use by 50% and saving 18,300 tCO₂/yr. Operated by Schroders Greencoat / Carlton Power.

label: EVREC Wind-to-H₂ (3+ GW, Newfoundland)
sub: Exploits Valley, Central Newfoundland, Canada. EDF-Abraxas JV (EVREC) filed EIS May 2026 for 3+ GW onshore wind-to-green hydrogen and ammonia project — one of Canada's largest. Targets 180,000 t/yr RFNBO hydrogen or 1 Mt/yr ammonia for export to Europe and Asia.

label: COP31 — Antalya (November 2026)
sub: Antalya, Türkiye. Upcoming COP31 (November 2026), chaired by Turkey's Murat Kurum. Copenhagen Ministerial (May 2026) designated electrification as the central COP31 deliverable — targeting 35% electricity share of final energy by 2035. Expected to advance the Global Stocktake and new NDC accountability mechanisms.

label: World Environment Day 2026 (Baku)
sub: Baku, Azerbaijan. Host of World Environment Day 2026 (June 5, 2026) — global ceremony at the Zaha Hadid-designed Heydar Aliyev Centre. Theme: 'A Global Call for Climate Action' (#NowForClimate). UN Secretary-General Guterres called for accelerated renewable energy transition; IUCN highlighted nature-based solutions for 30% of needed mitigation. Azerbaijan also hosted COP29 in November 2024.

label: SB64 Bonn Climate Talks
sub: Bonn, Germany. UNFCCC June Climate Meetings (SB64), June 8–18, 2026 — 9,206 registered participants. Gridlock on the Global Goal on Adaptation and Mitigation Work Programme, both deferred to COP31; progress on a 'Belém-Antalya' just transition mechanism package.

label: WA-CA-Québec Carbon Market Linkage
sub: Seattle, Washington, USA. Governor Bob Ferguson signed a carbon market linkage agreement with California and Québec on June 25, 2026, creating the world's largest subnational carbon market. Full linkage expected operational in 2027.

label: EU Solar Record (25% Share)
sub: Brussels / EU-wide. Solar generated a record 52 TWh (25% share) of EU electricity in June 2026 — for the first time, the bloc's single largest power source, ahead of nuclear, gas, wind, hydro and coal. Spain (34%), Germany (36%) and Poland (24%) led national shares (Ember, Jul 14, 2026).

label: East Anglia THREE Offshore Wind
sub: Suffolk coast, UK. ScottishPower Renewables and Masdar completed all 95 foundations for the £4bn, 1.4 GW East Anglia THREE offshore wind farm on August 17-18, 2026 -- set to power 1.3 million UK homes once operational by end of 2026.

label: Germany 128 GWp Solar Milestone
sub: Germany. Nationwide installed PV capacity surpassed 128 GWp in August 2026, hitting the statutory 2026 EEG expansion target ahead of schedule, per BSW-Solar analysis of Bundesnetzagentur data (announced Aug 20, 2026). Over 6 million solar installations now operating nationwide.
